events.title: Proximity Exhibition

venue.name: Snug Harbor Cultural Center
venue.address: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C)

events.description: Discover PROXIMITY, featuring 10 Snug Harbor studio artists across painting, photography & mixed media. Explore how shared spaces and creative con
events.details: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor's longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place-it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another. events.title: Community Recycling Event - Flushing
events.description: DSNY holds pop-up e-waste & textile recycling events in every Community Board district in New York City.
events.details: DSNY holds pop-up e-waste and textile recycling events in every Community Board district in New York City. E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), TVs, VCRs, DVDs, and DVRs, and all cords, cables, wiring accompanying e-waste devices. Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics. Unacceptable items: commercial waste, air conditioners, household appliances, batteries, lightbulbs. This event accepts paint in original containers, under 5 gallons (clear coatings, house paint, primers, stains, sealers). Learn more about this event.

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located in Tottenville on Staten Island
events.details: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies. Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp's great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance. It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. events.details: Join a knowledgeable Wave Hill Garden Guide for a leisurely stroll in the gardens. Garden Highlights Walks follow a variety of routes along mixed-material pathways and varying elevations. Accessible routes are available as requested; please indicate your need to the Garden Guide.
